items.title: Albert Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 24, 1997
items.q: his ten year collaboration with Count Basie resulted in Basie’s definitive biography Good Morning Blues.

ctx.x: Don’t think so. Well we have a couple of minutes before I know you have to move on. And I wanted to read one thing in your book from Basie, and just have you comment on it. This is something he said: “it’s the way you play it that makes it. What I say for Christ’s sakes, you don’t have to kill yourself to swing. Play like you play, play like you think, and then you got it, if you’re going to get it, and whatever you get, that’s you so that’s your story.” That was pretty much his philosophy on playing? That you…

Yeah. In other words he’s saying what is in your range, and you can extend yourself to see what your range is you see, then you don’t worry about what’s beyond that. Do the best you can within that. If you can do that then you’ve got it if you’re going to get it. If you’re not, you’re not. You see? So that he wasn’t likened to everything that came along at all. And sure enough, his stuff is, like I said right along, his is the durable stuff. And it turns out what he would use, let’s say there was bop. Basie was…
